name: Lamborghini Diablo SV
description:
Named after a legendary fighting bull known for its ferocity, the Lamborghini Diablo ('Devil' in Spanish) succeeded the iconic Countach in 1990 as Lamborghini's new flagship supercar. The original design brief was audacious: build a car capable of exceeding 315 km/h (196 mph), making it the fastest production car in the world. The Diablo delivered, briefly holding that title in 1991 with a verified top speed of 325 km/h.

In 1995, Lamborghini introduced the Diablo SV (Super Veloce - 'Super Fast'), a purist's dream that returned to the original rear-wheel-drive configuration after the standard Diablo had adopted all-wheel drive. The SV was more than just a drivetrain change—it represented a comprehensive performance upgrade focused on delivering the rawest, most visceral driving experience possible.

At the heart of the SV lies an enlarged and refined version of Lamborghini's legendary 5.7-liter V12 engine, now producing 510 horsepower at 7,000 rpm and 580 Nm of torque at 5,750 rpm. This naturally aspirated masterpiece breathes through revised intake and exhaust systems, while a dogleg 5-speed manual transmission sends all that power exclusively to the rear wheels—a setup that demands respect and rewards skill. The engine's operatic soundtrack, climbing through 7,000+ rpm, remains one of the most intoxicating sounds in automotive history.

The SV received distinctive visual updates that serve both form and function. Dual front fog lamps (replacing the standard car's quad setup) flank enlarged brake cooling ducts, while massive engine cover air intakes feed the hungry V12. A three-piece adjustable rear spoiler provides aerodynamic tuning capability, and optional SV side graphics announce the car's special status. The suspension was retuned for sharper responses, while larger brakes (330mm ventilated discs all around) provide the stopping power needed for a car capable of 340 km/h.

Weighing 1,530 kg and achieving 0-100 km/h in just 3.9 seconds, the Diablo SV represents the pinnacle of 1990s supercar engineering—a naturally aspirated, rear-wheel-drive, manual transmission V12 exotic from an era before electronic aids tamed the driving experience. It's a car that demands commitment and rewards mastery, embodying Lamborghini's philosophy of creating machines for those who truly know how to drive.
